AS A RESULT OF THE COVID-19 VIRUS, AND RESULTING ORDERS AND DIRECTION FROM THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES, THE GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, AND THE ORANGE COUNTY HEALTH CARE AGENCY, AS WELL AS THE CITY OF IRVINE EMERGENCY DECLARATION, THE PUBLIC WILL NOT BE PERMITTED TO PHYSICALLY ATTEND THE IRVINE CITY COUNCIL MEETING TO WHICH THIS AGENDA APPLIES.
YOU MAY SUBMIT COMMENTS ON ANY AGENDA ITEM OR ON ANY ITEM NOT ON THE AGENDA, IN WRITING VIA MAIL TO “ATTN: CITY COUNCIL,” ONE CIVIC CENTER PLAZA, IRVINE, CA 92606; BY EMAIL TO CLERK@CITYOFIRVINE.ORG; OR THROUGH E-COMMENT AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV. YOU MAY WATCH THE MEETING LIVE ON ICTV, COX COMMUNICATIONS LOCAL ACCESS CHANNEL 30, AND AT&T U-VERSE CHANNEL 99, AND LIVESTREAMED ONLINE AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV.
PLEASE NOTE: THE CITY COUNCIL IS MAKING EVERY EFFORT TO FOLLOW THE SPIRIT AND INTENT OF THE BROWN ACT AND OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS REGULATING THE CONDUCT OF PUBLIC MEETINGS, IN ORDER TO MAXIMIZE TRANSPARENCY AND PUBLIC ACCESS. IT WOULD BE APPRECIATED IF COMMUNICATIONS OF PUBLIC COMMENTS RELATED TO ITEMS ON THE AGENDA, OR ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA, ARE PROVIDED PRIOR TO THE COMMENCEMENT OF THE MEETING. IF THAT IS NOT POSSIBLE, EVERY EFFORT WILL BE MADE TO ATTEMPT TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS DURING THE COURSE OF THE MEETING. TOWARDS THIS END, THE MAYOR WILL ENDEAVOR TO TAKE A BRIEF PAUSE BEFORE ACTION IS TAKEN ON ANY AGENDA ITEM TO ALLOW THE CITY CLERK TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS, AND SHARE ANY E-COMMENTS RECEIVED DURING THE MEETING.

LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to the regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE

minutes_text:
MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  September 8, 2020
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:47 p.m. on September
8, 2020, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine,
California; Mayor Shea presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present:  5  Councilmember:  Melissa Fox
  Councilmember:  Farrah N. Khan
  Councilmember:  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor:  Mike Carroll
  Mayor:  Christina Shea

Mayor Shea announced that the meeting was broadcast live on Cox Communications Local
Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99, and livestreamed online at
cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public health and prevent the spread of
COVID-19, the e-comment feature had been extended for all agenda items, which allowed
members of the public the ability to submit e-comments through the public comment portion
of each item and would be included as part of the official record and uploaded to the City’s
website. She also assured the community that the City of Irvine was adhering to the
Governor’s Executive Order in the Council Chamber and throughout City Hall by sanitizing
surfaces and equipment, as well as wearing face masks.
 City Council Minutes  September 8, 2020

  She also reiterated that general public comments on items not on the agenda would be
  considered at approximately 6:30 p.m. or prior to adjournment, whichever occurred earlier,
  which had been standard practice prior to the COVID-19 pandemic; and expressed her
  appreciation for the community’s patience and understanding as adjustments to meeting
  protocols are made as needed.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Mayor Shea led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Pastor Jorge Molina from Mariners Church in Irvine provided the invocation.

  1.  CITY COUNCIL RECOGNITIONS

  1.1  Commendation Recognizing Frontline Medical Personnel

  Mayor Shea presented a commendation recognizing frontline medical
  personnel in the community, which included personnel from Hoag Hospital,
  Kaiser Permanente, St. Joseph Hospital, and UCI Medical Center, for their
  courage and selflessness during the COVID-19 pandemic.

  1.2  City Manager Recognition

  Mayor Shea recognized City Manager Russo for over 30 years in public
  service and as Irvine’s fifth City Manager; and presented a commendation
  and gifts. Scott Voigts and Deepak Sahni, on behalf of Orange County
  Supervisor and former Mayor Donald P. Wagner, also presented a
  resolution in recognition of City Manager Russo’s accomplishments and
  upcoming retirement.

  CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Khan welcomed new Irvine resident Mo Trafeh, a professional athlete,
  certified trainer, and running coach with almost 20 years of experience, and noted his
  numerous goals accomplishments over the years; and made the following announcement:

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  September 8, 2020

  •  California Clean Air Day is an educational project of the Coalition for Clean Air, and
  was built on the idea that shared experiences unite people to action to improve overall
  community health. The Clean Air Pledge allows individuals and organizations to do
  their part to clear the air through big and small actions. Those who participate will
  receive an item from the City that helps incorporate sustainability. The Clean Air
  Pledge runs from September 7 through Oct 7. For information on how to participate,
  visit cityofirvine.org/environmental programs or cleanair.org.

  Councilmember Kuo inquired about recent rolling blackouts in California and the City’s
  interface with Southern California Edison (SCE), to which Mike Hamel, Director of Public
  Safety/Chief of Police, provided a brief update, including recent communications with SCE;
  and announced the following:

  •  On Friday, September 11 at 8:30 a.m., the Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) will
  be livestreaming a brief ceremony commemorating 9/11. Due to COVID-19
  restrictions, the ceremony will be livestreamed on OCFA’s Facebook page at
  facebook.com/orangecountyfire.

  Mayor Shea made the following announcements:

  •  Hundreds of thousands of masks have been distributed throughout the community to
  stem the tide of COVID-19 and safeguard Irvine residents and workers. To help the
  community deliver critically important care and services as safely as possible and to
  protect the most vulnerable, masks have been provided to: 1) schools, childcare
  programs, and camps; 2) senior communities such as The Groves and The
  Meadows; 3) Irvine Community Land Trust communities; 4) Families Forward and
  Human Options; 5) skilled nursing facilities; and 6) Irvine businesses. Boxes of masks
  have also been provided to residents at events such as the Mask Giveaway at the
  Civic Center, the Great Park Farmers Market, and the Summer Drive-In Series
  events. Health and safety of the community will continue to be a top priority.
  Community members are reminded to wear a mask whenever out in the community
  and unable to maintain a distance of six feet from others.

  •  A feasibility study is being conducted to look at constructing a pedestrian bridge over
  Jamboree Road in the Irvine Business Complex (IBC), and members of the
  community are invited to provide input at a virtual open house on Thursday,
  September 10 from 5 to 6 p.m. There is a need for additional connections and new
  facilities for walking, bicycling, and recreation in the IBC, and the study will help
  identify and evaluate potential locations for the bridge along Jamboree Road between
  the 405 Freeway and Barranca Parkway. To register, visit cityofirvine.org.

  •  The Farmers Market event will safely return to its original format, and residents will
  be able to shop as a walk-up event, beginning Sunday, September 13. City staff are
  working with organizers of the Farmers Market to ensure that all relevant State and
  County guidelines are met. Masks and social distancing will be required. For
  information, visit ocgp.org/farmersmarket.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  September 8, 2020

  •  The 19th Annual Irvine Global Village Festival will look a little different, featuring three
  weeks of unique, interactive online experiences and two drive-in concerts. From
  September 21 through October 10, the community can enjoy the multicultural event
  through music, art, food, and fun in a safe and responsible manner, which includes:
  1) browsing photos and videos online to explore the history of the City’s fall festivals;
  2) making new memories from home with themed art classes and projects; 3) dining
  globally and supporting local restaurants; and 4) enjoying two drive-in concerts at the
  Orange County Great Park – True Willie and the Boys on September 25, and Mariachi
  Divas on October 10. For information, visit irvinefestival.org.

  •  Letters signed by Mayor Shea were sent to all Orange County cities seeking interest
  in joining a Community Choice Energy (CCE) program, and sharing participation
  costs with the City of Irvine. The cities of Costa Mesa, Fullerton, and Tustin expressed
  interest in talking further, and all have had additional questions. To respond to these
  questions, a Zoom meeting for all cities that would like to learn more about CCEs,
  pros and cons, costs, and savings, will be scheduled before the September 22 City
  Council meeting, with results shared at that meeting to determine next steps.

  •  Campaign signs related to Mayor Shea’s candidacy have recently been removed or
  damaged, and candidates are asked to be respectful of one another.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  2.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember Kuo, seconded by Vice Mayor Carroll,
  and unanimously carried to approve Consent Calendar Item Nos. 2.1, 2.2, 2.4,
  and 2.5. Consent Calendar Item Nos. 2.3, 2.6, and 2.7 were removed for separate
  discussion.

  2.1  MINUTES

  ACTION:
  1) Approved the minutes of a special meeting of the Irvine City
  Council held on July 28, 2020.
  2) Approved the minutes of a regular meeting of the Irvine City
  Council and regular joint meeting with the City of Irvine as
  Successor Agency to the dissolved Irvine Redevelopment Agency
  held on July 28, 2020.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Minutes  September 8, 2020

  2.2  WARRANTS AND WIRE TRANSFER RESOLUTION

  ACTION:
  Adopted RESOLUTION NO. 20-70 - A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA, ALLOWING
  CERTAIN CLAIMS AND DEMANDS AND SPECIFYING THE
  FUNDS OUT OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO BE PAID

  2.3  PROCLAMATIONS

  Molly Perry, City Clerk, noted that an e-comment had been received by
  Anonymous Resident, who suggested that the Public Information Office
  post information daily about Constitution and Citizenship Day during
  Constitution Week on the City’s social media sites.

  There was no City Council discussion.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Kuo, seconded by Vice Mayor
  Carroll, and unanimously carried to:

  Proclaim September 17, 2020, as Daughters of the American
  Revolution’s "Constitution Day and Citizenship Day"; and September
  17-23, 2020, as "Constitution Week."

  2.4  ACCEPTANCE OF CARES ACT FUNDING FOR SENIOR SERVICES
  PROGRAMMING

  ACTION:
  1) Authorized the City Manager to execute contract for acceptance
  of Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act (CARES
  Act) funding in the amount of $231,643 from the County of Orange
  Office on Aging for Senior Services programming. (Contract No.
  11174)
  2) Approved Budget Adjustment to increase revenues and
  expenditures in the amount of $231,643 in Fiscal Year 2020-21.

  2.5  DEFINED BENEFIT AND DEFINED CONTRIBUTION PENSION PLAN
  AUDITS FOR THE YEAR ENDED DECEMBER 31, 2019

  ACTION:
  Received and filed the Defined Benefit and the Defined Contribution
  Pension Plan audits for the year ended December 31, 2019.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  5
 City Council Minutes  September 8, 2020

  2.6  ACCEPTANCE OF MARUCHAN, INC. DONATION

  Molly Perry, City Clerk, noted that the following e-comments had been
  received:

  •  Anonymous Resident, who expressed appreciation to Maruchan,
  Inc., for its contribution and generosity to the community.

  •  Clownstina Shea and Jonathan Beer, who expressed opposition
  and suggested the donation be directed from the Police Department
  to another City department.

  Mayor Shea expressed her appreciation to Maruchan, Inc., for its
  continued generosity over the years.

  ACTION: Moved by Vice Mayor Carroll, seconded by Councilmember
  Kuo, and unanimously carried to:

  1) Accept a $100,000 donation from Maruchan, Inc.
  2) Approve a budget adjustment appropriating $100,000, reflecting
  an increase in revenues and appropriations.

  2.7  NOTICE OF REVIEW FOR A TRACT MAP IN CYPRESS VILLAGE

  Molly Perry, City Clerk, noted that an e-comment had been received from
  Anonymous Resident, who inquired about the September 3, 2020,
  Planning Commission meeting and requested a copy of the recording.

  There was no City Council discussion.

  ACTION: Moved by Vice Mayor Carroll, seconded by Councilmember
  Kuo, and unanimously carried to:

  Receive and file.

  3.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  3.1  ZONING ORDINANCE UPDATE – ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS

  Mayor Shea opened the public hearing at 5:33 p.m.

  Marika Poynter, Principal Planner, presented the staff report and
  responded to questions.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  6
 City Council Minutes  September 8, 2020

  City Council discussion included questioning whether staff had been in
  contact with the State’s housing division regarding the proposed changes.

  Councilmember Fox reiterated her opposition to the proposed Ordinance
  despite recent changes made by the Planning Commission.

  Molly Perry, City Clerk, noted that the following e-comments had been
  received:

  •  Jose Trinidad Castaneda, who expressed support of the proposed
  revisions.

  •  Matthew Gelfand, on behalf of Californians for Homeownership,
  who expressed opposition, noting that Irvine would be the only city
  in California to defy the state’s accessory dwelling unit laws.

  By consensus, Mayor Shea closed the public hearing at 5:40 p.m.

  ACTION: Moved by Vice Mayor Carroll, seconded by Mayor Shea, to:

  Introduce for first reading and read by title only ORDINANCE NO. 20-
  06 – AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  IRVINE, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING A ZONE CHANGE (00822886-
  PZC) TO AMEND THE CITY’S ZONING ORDINANCE BY
  PROVIDING NEW OR REVISED PROVISIONS RELATED TO
  ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS; FILED BY THE CITY OF IRVINE
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT

  The motion carried as follows:

  AYES:  4 COUNCILMEMBERS:  Carroll, Khan, Kuo, and Shea

  NOES:  1 COUNCILMEMBERS:  Fox

  ABSENT:  0 COUNCILMEMBERS:  None

  3.2  DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT STATUS REPORT

  Mayor Shea opened the public hearing at 5:41 p.m.

  Diane Vu, Senior Planner, presented the staff report and responded to
  questions.

  City Council discussion included confirming whether all existing
  development agreements were in compliance with their respective terms
  and conditions.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  7
 City Council Minutes  September 8, 2020

  Molly Perry, City Clerk, noted that no e-comments were received on this
  item.

  By consensus, Mayor Shea closed the public hearing at 5:45 p.m.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Kuo, seconded by Mayor Shea,
  and unanimously carried to:

  Find all active City Development Agreements in compliance with their
  respective terms and conditions.

  4.  COUNCIL BUSINESS

  4.1  AGREEMENT FOR EMPLOYMENT OF MARIANNA MARYSHEVA AS
  INTERIM CITY MANAGER OF THE CITY OF IRVINE

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, presented the staff report and responded to
  questions.

  City Council discussion included noting that the terms and conditions of the
  proposed agreement would result in an overall cost savings.

  Molly Perry, City Clerk, noted that an e-comment was received by
  Anonymous Resident, who spoke in support of Assistant City Manager
  Marysheva serving as Interim City Manager.

  ACTION: Moved by Mayor Shea, seconded by Councilmember Kuo,
  and unanimously carried to:

  Approve Agreement for Employment of Interim City Manager
  between City of Irvine and Marianna Marysheva. (Contract No.
  11175)

  4.2  COVID-19 SITUATIONAL UPDATE AND DIRECTION TO DIRECTOR OF
  EMERGENCY SERVICES ON RELEVANT ACTION ITEMS, INCLUDING
  EXTENSION OF CITY ORDERS

  Marianna Marysheva, Assistant City Manager, presented the staff report
  and responded to questions. Melissa Haley, Manager of Public

  4.3  DISCUSSION OF PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN IRVINE CITY COUNCIL
  AND COMMISSION MEETINGS DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC

  This item was considered following Council Business Item Nos. 4.4 and
  4.5.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  9
 City Council Minutes  September 8, 2020

  Molly Perry, City Clerk, presented the staff report and responded to
  questions. Khaled Tawfik, Chief Information Officer, was also available for
  questions.

  Carl Petersen, Assistant City Clerk, noted that an e-comment was received
  by Anonymous Resident, who expressed support for the current options
  afforded the public and expressed support for communication of all
  mediums being provided in an equal manner.

  City Council discussion included: questioning the financial impacts of
  additional staff time to manage public speakers; inquired about necessary
  safety and social distancing measures; questioned whether members of
  the public would be limited to only providing public comments or had the
  option of attending an entire meeting; inquired about liability waivers and
  their enforceability; questioned whether those who refuse to sign a waiver
  could still participate; inquired about whether the e-comment platform was
  compliant with the temporary provisions of the Brown Act; noted the
  increase in participation through the e-comment system; discussed the
  pros and cons of additional mechanisms for public participation; and
  suggested that the City Clerk expand research to the County as well as
  special districts, including the Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) and
  Transportation Corridor Agencies (TCA), and return to the City Council at
  the first meeting in October with updated State guidelines and a draft
  waiver for consideration.

  City Attorney Melching reiterated the provisions of the Governor’s
  Executive Order, which required cities provide opportunity for members of
  the public to observe and participate in meetings, and because other
  mechanisms were available to the public (e-comment, e-mail, etc.),
  members of the public could be required to sign a waiver if they chose to
  participate in person; and noted that a liability waiver should be sufficient if
  a person has options and they are well informed about the risks of in-
  person attendance.

  No action was taken.

  This item was agendized at the request of Councilmembers Fox and Khan,
  who asked for City Council support to adopt a resolution urging the United
  States Postmaster General to end all actions that slow down or undermine
  the prompt delivery of mail services.

  City Council discussion included: questioning the approximate number of
  U.S. mailboxes and sorting machines that had been removed to date;
  noted recent delays in mail delivery, including the delivery of
  pharmaceuticals; expressed concern about the intention of the resolution
  and taking a position on a state and federal matter; and suggested a letter
  be sent to the U.S. Postmaster General in lieu of a resolution to include a
  request to remedy actions already taken, including restoring equipment
  and related services.

  Molly Perry, City Clerk, noted that the following e-comments had been
  received expressing support for the adoption of the proposed resolution:

  •  Anonymous Resident
  •  Debra Mathias
  •  Howard Roll

  ACTION: Moved by Mayor Shea, seconded by Vice Mayor Carroll, and
  unanimously carried to:

  ACTION:
  Send a letter to the U.S. Postmaster General urging the ending of
  actions that slow down or undermine the prompt delivery of the U.S.
  mail, ensuring that delivery of U.S. mail is prompt, safe, and secure,
  especially during the COVID-19 pandemic and the U.S. Presidential
  Election, and remedying actions already taken, including restoring
  equipment and related services.
